_doc: Failure pattern taxonomy. After each eval result, loop driver tests each pattern's 'if' condition; matched patterns produce candidate rule additions. Agent reviews + accepts/rejects in next iteration.

patterns.interpretation: Direct physical pruning without any recovery module is structurally invalid at this compression level.
patterns.add_rule_template: Direct pruning of {k}+ layers requires a recovery module; do not propose direct recovery for k>={k} again.

patterns.trigger_if: sr drops by >10pt when a specific layer is added to the mask compared to a near-twin mask without that layer (same recovery)
patterns.interpretation: The added layer is a functional anchor whose removal disrupts pipeline.
patterns.add_rule_template: L{layer_idx} is a functional anchor for {suite}; do not include in mask without explicit ablation justification.

patterns.interpretation: Adapter alone cannot fully compensate for deeper pruning; action interface needs co-adaptation.
patterns.add_rule_template: For mask_size>={k}, propose joint recovery (adapter + action_head + proprio) instead of adapter_only.

patterns.interpretation: Mask + recovery combination achieves dense-level performance; structure is validated.
patterns.add_rule_template: Mask {mask_summary} with {recovery} reaches dense-level SR for {suite}; record as validated configuration.

patterns.trigger_if: static proxy (FIM/CKA) ranks a layer as removable BUT closed-loop SR shows >5pt drop when removed
patterns.interpretation: Static proxy missed a functional role only visible in closed-loop execution.
patterns.add_rule_template: L{layer_idx} is closed-loop-critical despite low static score; distrust static-only rankings for this suite.

patterns.trigger_if: two iterations with same recovery have masks differing by <=2 layers AND |sr_a - sr_b| > 0.10
patterns.interpretation: The small mask difference (<=2 layers) drives a large SR jump; the differing layers are anchor candidates. Generalizes anchor_violation to bidirectional swaps and 2-layer diffs (e.g., the L30 cliff at k=28 vs k=29).
patterns.add_rule_template: Layers {differing_layers} produce SR cliff {sr_lower:.2f}->{sr_higher:.2f} (Delta={delta:.2f}pt) between near-twin masks; treat as anchor candidates.

patterns.interpretation: Soft warning: agent jumped k aggressively without consolidating wins at smaller k first. Methodology says: sweep at k=K to find best start, push k by +4..+8 once SR is solid. Skipping ahead may bypass important calibration.
patterns.add_rule_template: Soft warning: k={current_k} jumps >8 layers beyond prior max k={max_k_seen} while best SR={max_sr:.2f} (< 0.85). Consider consolidating at smaller k first.

patterns.trigger_if: current mask KEEPS a layer with training_free_sr >= 0.85 AND REMOVES a layer with training_free_sr < 0.50
patterns.interpretation: The agent's mask choice contradicts per-layer training-free SR evidence: kept layer is individually easy to remove, while removed layer is individually a hard anchor. Suggests a potential swap. Soft signal — recovery training MAY rescue hard anchors, but the priority is reversed.
patterns.add_rule_template: INVERTED anchor priority: kept L{kept_L}(tf-SR={kept_sr:.2f}) is easily-removable while removed L{removed_L}(tf-SR={removed_sr:.2f}) is a hard anchor. Consider swap.
